turn.content:
The records are clear. Let me confirm the picture:

- **PO-2026-0278** ordered 2 of each line (2× cleaning service, 2× trash bags, 6× air fresheners).
- Two goods receipts exist: **GR-2026-0278A** (2026-10-10) and **GR-2026-0278B** (2026-10-23), each for 1 cleaning service, 1 trash bag pack, 3 air fresheners — i.e. the PO was split into two deliveries.
- **MHL26100409** (2026-10-11, total 8,670,543) was raised one day after the first receipt, so it billed delivery A.
- This invoice **MHL26100417** (2026-10-26), with identical amount, bills qty 1/1/3 — the contents of the second receipt, delivery B.
- `get_billing_position` for PO-2026-0278: value_received_with_tax 17,341,086 vs invoiced_including_this 17,341,086, `within_received: true` — the two invoices together exactly exhaust the received value, no line being billed twice.

That distinguishes `separate_delivery` (within received) from `resubmission` (not within received).
